name: Intercom
description: Inter-session communication and presence. Lets any session see what other sessions are doing (live roster with derived liveness, plus deep inspection of a peer's tasks, background jobs, and sub-agent fleet) and message them (note, ping, interrupt, or broadcast). Messages are durable, pull-delivered as a per-turn <ma::agent::intercom-inbox> block, and crash/resume safe; ping/interrupt wake an idle peer between turns. Tools: Peers, Send, Inbox. Disable presence with MINIMAL_AGENT_INTERCOM_NO_PRESENCE=1.

tool.name: Peers
tool.description: See other minimal-agent sessions running on this machine and what they are doing. action:"list" (the default) returns the live roster: every messageable peer with its short id, derived liveness (online, idle, busy, stale, hung, dead, or offline), model, cwd, and current activity. action:"inspect" deep-dives one peer, gathering its task list, background jobs, sub-agent fleet, recent activity, and a transcript excerpt from across plugins. Liveness is derived from heartbeat freshness plus a pid probe, so a session that crashed without exiting cleanly still reads as stale, hung, or dead instead of falsely online. Pass liveOnly:true to drop gone sessions from the list. Read-only. Example: Peers({action:"inspect", peer:"a1b2c3d4", include:["tasks","activity"]}).

action.description: "list" (default) for the roster, or "inspect" for a deep dive on one peer.

peer.description: inspect: which peer to look at. A short id (e.g. "a1b2c3d4"), a full session id, or an at-mention. Required for inspect.

include.description: inspect: which sections to gather. Default [tasks, activity, jobs]. Add "fleet" for sub-agents, "transcript" for a recent transcript excerpt.

liveOnly.description: list: drop dead/offline sessions, showing only reachable peers. Default false.

tool.name: Send
tool.description: Send a message to another minimal-agent session: a note, a ping, an interrupt, or a broadcast. Use it to hand off a result, claim a shared resource, flag a blocker, or ask a peer to stop. `to` is a peer short id or full session id, or "all" to reach every reachable session, or "project" for sessions that share your project directory. `kind` defaults to "note", which is passive and waits in the peer's inbox until their next turn; "ping" also wakes an idle peer between turns; "interrupt" wakes them and signals urgency. Messages are durable and survive crashes and resumes, and the recipient sees your identity (short id, model, cwd). You cannot send to yourself. Run Peers first to see who is online. Example: Send({to:"a1b2c3d4", body:"finished the auth refactor, your turn on the API"}).

to.description: Recipient: a peer short id like "a1b2c3d4" or a full session id, or "all" to broadcast to every reachable peer, or "project" for peers in your project directory.

body.description: The message text. Keep it short and self-contained: the recipient has none of your context, so say who you are and what you need.

kind.description: Delivery urgency. "note" (default) is passive and waits for the peer's next turn. "ping" wakes an idle peer between turns. "interrupt" wakes them and signals urgency. Prefer note unless latency matters.

replyTo.description: Optional prior message id this replies to (threading, display-only).

tool.name: Inbox
tool.description: Re-read intercom messages you have already received. New messages are delivered to you automatically each turn as a <ma::agent::intercom-inbox> block, so you rarely need this tool. Reach for it to review history or to double-check after the fact. scope:"unread" (the default) shows messages since your last Inbox read. scope:"recent" shows the latest messages regardless. Reading here never hides the automatic per-turn delivery. Example: Inbox({scope:"recent", limit:10}).

scope.description: "unread" (default) since your last Inbox read, or "recent" for the latest messages.
